new.description: the Runner type — run, runAtBase, lanes
the vitest runner the package ships
the three operations, driven over the real reporter's output

summary: Seed harness/ with the Runner interface — run, runAtBase, lanes — and the vitest runner behind it, each operation returning structured results rather than exit codes.
tests: the vitest runner reports, per named line, whether one passing test carried it
the vitest runner lays the merged bytes over a detached base checkout and runs the same names there
the vitest runner reports its lanes and the files each excludes
pins: no module under src/ imports harness/
acceptance: harness/vitestRunner.ts satisfies harness/runner.ts's three operations with structured per-name results, and pnpm tsc --noEmit + pnpm test are green.
notes: Port from .flume/vitestJudge.ts, keeping its posture: pure over the reporter's own output, so the real writer drives the real reader. `lanes` is the mechanism the open vitest-lane question wants — the runner declares its lanes, the judge refuses at plan time. The chain-side copy retires at the cutover (open-questions, the phase-lane question).

summary: Ship harness/ as the ./harness subpath of @dtmd/flume — one package, one version, one exports map — and extend the install acceptance to resolve it.
tests: the package exports map resolves ./harness to the built harness entry point
the build tsconfig emits harness/ beside src/
acceptance: pnpm build emits dist/harness/index.js, the exports map resolves @dtmd/flume/harness to it, and pnpm run smoke:install resolves the subpath from the installed tarball.
notes: The fence, the typecheck include, and the sweep domain already name harness/ (0c93bd4); the published surface is what is missing. smoke-install runs outside the fast lane, so the two named behaviors read the manifests and the smoke step rides acceptance.

new.description: the strict declaration schema and its refusal

edit.description: export the schema and its type

summary: Add the package's strict declaration schema — the eleven fields a consumer declares — refusing an unknown or a missing required field at load, naming the field and the valid set.
tests: the declaration schema parses a declaration naming every field
an unknown declaration field is refused, naming the field and the valid set
a missing required declaration field is refused, naming the field
acceptance: harness/declaration.ts parses a full declaration and refuses both an unknown field and a missing required one, each refusal naming the field.
notes: runner types against harness/runner.ts. No field names an engine artifact path, a verdict field, or a prior-attempt mode — those are the engine's to report. This entry is the shape alone; its consumers are the cite resolver and the chain factory, later entries.

new.description: per resolution against specLocus, resolver declarable
the two refusals and the declared resolver

edit.description: export the resolver and its verdict type

summary: Add the package's per resolver: the path matches a specLocus glob and is in the gated commit, the section is a heading in it, and a consumer may declare a resolver that keys sections instead.
tests: a per cite whose path matches no specLocus glob is refused, naming the path
a per cite whose section is no heading at the gated commit is refused, naming the section
a declared resolver keys a section without changing the verdict shape
acceptance: harness/citeResolver.ts resolves a per against a declared specLocus at a commit and yields one verdict shape whether the section is found by heading or by a declared resolver.
notes: The at-ref reader is injected, not imported, so every case stays in the fast lane. .flume/chain.ts's perResolvesGate and sectionOf are the chain-side copy this retires at the cutover.
